AWPTCM-T33300.objective:
• MAC address thrashing protection is enabled by default and detects rapid MAC address movement indicative of a loop.
  • Thrashing protection can be configured with different actions on detection: learn-disable, link-down, port-disable, vlan-disable, or none (with optional timeout).
  • When the configured action triggers, the affected port or VLAN is placed in the appropriate state (e.g. link-down, learning disabled, or VLAN disabled on the port) and the reason is logged.
  • Show commands (e.g. show interface switchport) correctly report which VLANs or ports are currently experiencing MAC thrashing.
  • MAC thrashing protection functions correctly on G.8032 interfaces (R-APS messages may require higher thrash limits to avoid false triggers).
  • Protection works across LAGs/static channels (treated appropriately) and in stacked environments.
  • Protection interoperates with related features such as LDF and UFO without overriding their decisions incorrectly.

steps.description: Note: Related ART Tests linked in Traceability. Primary coverage from TestLink MAC Thrashing family (AWP-18040 primary, AWP-18059, AWP-26054 G.8032 interop, AWP-7460 CLI show, AWP-7470/1 LAG info, AWP-13785 combo tests). ART coverage from 1346.1001.95 (MAC thrashing link-down detection + action + logging) and nearby loop protection cases.
Verify MAC thrashing protection is enabled by default. Induce rapid MAC movement (loop) between ports and confirm detection occurs with appropriate logging.
Configure thrash-limit with action learn-disable (and timeout). Trigger thrashing and verify learning is disabled on the affected port/VLAN and it logs the event.
Repeat for other actions: link-down, port-disable, vlan-disable. Confirm the port or VLAN enters the expected state and recovers after timeout if configured.
Configure action none (log only) and verify thrashing is detected and logged without disabling the port or learning.
Issue show interface switchport (and related commands) while thrashing is active. Confirm the output accurately identifies the thrashing VLANs/ports.
Configure on G.8032 ring interfaces (with suitable high thrash-limit). Induce ring breaks/restores and confirm MAC thrashing protection functions without disrupting G.8032 operation.
Test on LAG interfaces and in a stack. Confirm thrashing is detected and action applied correctly (LAG treated as logical unit where appropriate).
